subject: Discovery Recap: Tool Calling & Structured Output (JSON schema)
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 28 Jun 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery Recap: Tool Calling & Structured Output (JSON schema)

Hi Samantha —

Thanks again for taking time today to walk through Acme Health’s use case. As promised, below is a concise recap of the call, agreed pain points, and proposed next steps so we’re all aligned. Please let me know if I missed anything.

1) Key pain points you shared
- Need deterministic, machine-readable outputs from agents for downstream integrations (billing, claims ingestion).
- Current LLM output variability causes manual QA and mapping work downstream.
- Existing stack includes in-house rules engine + a fine-tuned LLM hosted via vendor X; throughput and cost are concerns.

2) Current stack & constraints
- Data flow: EHR -> ETL -> rules engine -> human QA -> downstream systems.
- Constraints: PHI protection (in-region processing only), predictable latency (<300ms p50 for light requests), and strict JSON schema enforcement for ingestion.

3) Success criteria for an initial pilot
- Agent outputs validate against a fixed JSON schema with zero schema validation errors for >95% of test prompts.
- End-to-end latency under 500ms for single-turn tool-calling flows in pilot environment.
- Clear unit economics: target token cost < $0.005 per response average.

4) Tool/function calling & structured output needs we discussed
- Agent should call a single validated tool endpoint with deterministic JSON body for each recognized intent.
- We recommended embedding a validation step and strict output formatter layer (examples attached).
- Example deterministic formatting success criteria: always include top-level keys ["patient_id","action","payload"]; arrays must be fixed-schema; no free-text in payload fields except explicit note fields.

5) Attachments referenced
- discovery-json-schema-draft.json (attached) — example schema we drafted in the meeting.
- Sample agent workflow diagram (link in follow-ups).

6) Next steps (agreed)
- Redwood: provide a short pilot proposal and pricing estimate for a 6-week pilot (deliverables: schema validator, agent config, test harness). Will include infrastructure notes for in-region processing and data handling. (Action: Jordan — by Tue 6/30)
- Acme: share a small prompt/testset and security questionnaire (Action: Samantha)
- Joint: schedule a walkthrough of the validation harness + schema enforcement (Action: Lauren to coordinate possible times next week)

Quick sample of the deterministic output pattern we discussed (pseudo):

-- begin sample --
{
  "patient_id": "123456",
  "action": "submit_claim",
  "payload": {
    "claim_items": [ { "code": "ABC123", "amount": 123.45 } ],
    "notes": "structured-only: allow free text only in notes field"
  }
}
-- end sample --

Attachment: discovery-json-schema-draft.json (application/json)

Thanks — looking forward to the next steps.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0147

Subject: Re: Discovery Recap: Tool Calling & Structured Output (JSON schema)

Jordan —

Appreciate the clear recap, and yes this matches our notes. Couple quick clarifications and asks:

- Success criteria: the 95% schema pass rate is fine as a starting target; for production we’ll need to get to 99% with an explicit human-in-loop gating flow.
- PHI handling: we need a plan for in-region key management (KMS) and audit logs — can you include options for KMS/HSM and audit retention in the pilot proposal?
- Pilot scope: we’ll start with two endpoints (claims submission, patient-update). Will share a 50-prompt test set by tomorrow.

I’ve attached our security questionnaire and a short doc that lists the data fields we need in the JSON.

Also curious on pricing: please include a ballpark for a limited pilot (6 weeks, up to 50k tokens) and an option for Dedicated capacity if the pilot looks promising.

Thanks — I’ll send the test prompts this afternoon.

Best,
Samantha Lee
Head of Integrations
Acme Health
samantha@acmehealth.com
